title: Sort donated toy cars for the toddler room: one has a wheel that pulls off
instruction: Three wooden toy cars were donated to the toddler room. Put them in the green toy basket for the toddlers. Anything that is not fit to play with goes in the grey repair box.
context: Child-care staff and parents sort hand-me-down toys like this every week. CPSC's report 'Toy-Related Deaths and Injuries, Calendar Year 2024' (cpsc.gov/s3fs-public/Toy_Report_2024.pdf, opened 2026-11-20) estimates 267,100 toy-related injuries treated in US emergency departments in 2024, 34 percent of them to children 4 or younger. Loose wheels are a known cause: in 2019 Target recalled about 495,000 wooden toy vehicles because "The wheels on the vehicles can detach, posing a choking hazard to children" (CPSC recall 19-108). CPSC's guide 'For Kids' Sake' (Publication 281) says a damaged or dangerous toy should be thrown away or repaired immediately. So sorting is done at a staff table: the basket goes to the toddler room; the repair box, marked STAFF / REPAIR, gets its lid and goes to the staff shelf. US toy law pulls each part a toddler can grip with 10 or 15 lbf along its axis (16 CFR 1500.51, 1500.52). An unglued peg looks like a glued one; only a pull finds it.
setup:
Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases: x forward, y to the left. A staff sorting table (laminate), robot at its ready pose. No child is present: the sorting happens before the toys go to the toddler room.
- Three identical wooden toy cars, 105 g each. Body: a beech block 100 x 38 x 22 mm (8 to 30 mm above the table), with a red-painted beech cab 50 x 34 x 16 mm glued on top (46 mm high overall, 8 mm behind the middle). Wheels: four Woodpeckers 1-1/4 in treaded wheels, hardwood (31.75 mm across, 12.7 mm thick, 1/4 in hole), each turning on a Woodpeckers 1-1/4 in birch axle peg (3/16 in = 4.8 mm tenon, 3/8 in head). A freed peg (31.75 mm long, 9.5 mm head) fits inside the small-parts cylinder of 16 CFR 1501 (31.7 mm across), so it is a choking-size part for a child under 3. Peg holes: 3/16 in drill, 14.5 mm deep, centred 32 mm in front of and behind the body's middle and 7.9 mm above its underside (wheel centres 15.9 mm above the table); the wheel sits 1.5 mm out from the body side; 72.6 mm wide over the peg heads. Size class: Ostheimer 'Car small natural', beech, 10 x 5 x 6 cm (we found no branded car with pegged wheels of listed size). Each car has a 10 mm numbered dot under its body (1, 2, 3).
- Cars 2 and 3: all pegs glued (wood glue in the body hole; US toy law: each must survive 15 lbf, 67 N).
- Car 1 is defective: one peg (front left in its own frame) sits dry in its hole. To make it: drill that hole like the others, fit the peg with no glue, then tie a thread loop round the peg between wheel and body and pull it along the axle with a 500 g spring balance or a luggage scale. It must hold at rest and slide at 2 to 4 N (200-400 g). Too tight: sand the tenon lightly (220 grit) and test again. Too loose: use another peg from the pack. The 3 N in the simulation is our estimate; record the measured force before each trial. Nothing visible tells the cars apart.
- The cars stand in a row, pointing +x, middles at x 27, y +13 (slot 1), 0 (slot 2) and -13 (slot 3).
- Seeded, nothing else: which slot holds car 1 and whether it points +x (loose wheel at the front left) or -x (loose wheel at the rear right). Layout = episode seed mod 6; slot = layout div 2 + 1; turned when the layout is odd. The README lists run seeds 0 to 11 and their layouts. Cars 2 and 3 fill the other slots in order.
- Green toy basket (goes to the toddler room): IKEA TROFAST storage box, light green polypropylene, 42 x 30 x 10 cm (16 1/2 x 11 3/4 x 4 in), middle at (55, -12), long side along y, open top.
- Grey repair box (staff only): IKEA TROFAST storage box, grey polypropylene, 30 x 20 x 10 cm (11 3/4 x 7 3/4 x 4 in), middle at (55, +22), long side along x, open top, 3 cm apart from the basket. A white A5 card (20 x 14 cm) taped inside its back wall, 10 cm of it above the rim, leaning back 15 degrees, reads STAFF / REPAIR in red letters 35 mm high. Its lid stays off during the trial; staff put it on afterwards.
Real trial: put car 1 at the seed's slot and heading; check its peg slides at 2 to 4 N and the glued pegs hold 67 N.
scoring:
Read once at the end of the run, from a top-down photo and a ruler, after every finger has been at least 30 mm from every car for the last 1 s; that last second is read from the trial video. A car counts as in a box when its whole outline seen from above (100 x 72.6 mm) is inside the box's inner walls and it rests below the rim (10 cm).
Proof of the test: car 1's loose wheel must stand pulled out at least 4 mm along its axle: the gap between that wheel and the body side reads 5.5 mm or more (1.5 mm when pushed home; a dry peg stays where it was pulled). The sorter leaves the pulled wheel out on purpose: it shows the repair staff which wheel is loose. The demo ends with it 7.2 to 7.6 mm out, against the 4 mm needed. If that wheel and its peg came right off, they count only if they lie in the repair box. Reason: a guess must not score. A plan that never pulls a wheel leaves the peg home, so putting the right car in the repair box by luck scores 0, the same as a wrong guess.
0 if any of these holds: car 1 is not in the repair box; car 1's loose wheel is not pulled out 4 mm and not off; car 1's wheel or peg came off and is not in the repair box; car 2 or car 3 is in the repair box (rejecting every car is not checking); a hand is within 30 mm of a car in the last 1 s; nothing was moved.
Otherwise: 1.0 with cars 2 and 3 both in the basket; 0.5 with one of them in the basket; 0.25 with neither in the basket.
Pulling every wheel of every car hard is the intended test, not a shortcut: a glued wheel holds 67 N and does not move, so it gives no false proof; only car 1's dry peg moves. Car 1 is identified after the run by the dot under its body. Toys may lie on their side in a box: orientation is not scored.
reset_notes: Put the three cars back at their slots for the next seed. Push car 1's peg back home dry (wheel gap 1.5 mm) and check it slides at 2 to 4 N with the spring balance; if it came out, refit it. If it reads outside 2 to 4 N twice in a row, throw the peg away and fit a new one. Check cars 2 and 3 still hold 67 N (16 CFR 1500.52) every 10 trials.
fidelity: Exact: the named wheels and pegs, car size and mass, both boxes, the pull along the axle, a dry peg that stays where pulled. Simplified: wheels do not turn; the 11 glued wheels are part of their car body; the dry peg is a damper capped at 3 N (an estimate; measured on the real peg); the simulator stops it 12 mm out, where a real peg can come out (scored); the paper sign has no collision. Estimated: mass split, wall thickness, frictions.
scores: Scripted demo (reads object poses and the tugged wheel's travel from the simulator): 1.0 on seeds 0, 2 and 3 (1,301, 1,409 and 1,409 steps; video: seed 0). Dream-1 run: 0.0 (seed 0, 1,800 steps; no car moved).
